citations.quote: The capabilities interaction retrieves the information about a server's capabilities - which portions of this specification it supports.

claims.text: The /metadata response arrived in 286 milliseconds from a single vantage point (davis-ca/residential), earning the endpoint full marks for response speed.

citations.quote: Applications SHALL return a resource that describes the functionality of the server end-point.

The FHIR specification defines fhirVersion as a required field, noting it records the 'FHIR Version the system supports.'

claims.text: The CapabilityStatement does not include a software name or version. The FHIR specification provides an optional software element with a required name child: 'A name the software is known by.' Because this element is absent, the transparency check for software identity failed, costing 20 of 100 transparency points.

citations.quote: <name value="[string]"/><!-- 1..1 A name the software is known by -->

claims.text: The CapabilityStatement lists 26 resource types, and 25 of those 26 document their supported interactions. The FHIR specification states that servers 'SHALL specify what resource types and operations are supported,' so documenting interactions for nearly all declared resources is consistent with that requirement.

citations.quote: Servers SHALL specify what resource types and operations are supported, and SHOULD also specify profiles for each resource type.

claims.text: The CapabilityStatement declares US Core, CARIN, and Da Vinci profiles. US Core is an implementation guide based on FHIR R4 that 'defines the minimum constraints on the FHIR resources to create the US Core Profiles' and is designed to promote interoperability and adoption through common implementation.

citations.quote: The US Core Implementation Guide is based on FHIR Version R4. It defines the minimum constraints on the FHIR resources to create the US Core Profiles.

claims.text: A SMART discovery document — the JSON file that SMART App Launch (an OAuth-based authorization layer for FHIR) requires at /.well-known/smart-configuration — was found and is complete. The SMART specification states that 'FHIR endpoints requiring authorization SHALL serve a JSON document at the location formed by appending /.well-known/smart-configuration to their base URL.' In addition, the CapabilityStatement itself declares an OAuth/SMART security service, visible in the security section where supported services include 'OAuth | SMART-on-FHIR.'

citations.quote: FHIR endpoints requiring authorization SHALL serve a JSON document at the location formed by appending /.well-known/smart-configuration to their base URL.

claims.text: US Core (a set of FHIR profiles defining minimum data requirements for US patient data interoperability), CARIN, and Da Vinci profiles are declared in the CapabilityStatement, earning full marks (40/40) for the interoperability profile check.

citations.quote: The US Core Implementation Guide is based on FHIR Version R4. It defines the minimum constraints on the FHIR resources to create the US Core Profiles.

claims.text: The SMART App Launch well-known configuration document was absent or incomplete. SMART (Substitutable Medical Applications and Reusable Technologies) App Launch requires that 'FHIR endpoints requiring authorization SHALL serve a JSON document at the location formed by appending /.well-known/smart-configuration to their base URL.' This check did not pass, resulting in 0/35 points for that dimension. Additionally, no OAuth security service was declared in the CapabilityStatement's security section, which can list services such as 'OAuth | SMART-on-FHIR | NTLM | Basic | Kerberos | Certificates,' resulting in 0/25 points for that check.

citations.quote: FHIR endpoints requiring authorization SHALL serve a JSON document at the location formed by appending /.well-known/smart-configuration to their base URL.
